# windows_net_route (Data Source)

Reads the observed state of an existing persistent route on a remote Windows host without managing it. Typical use: `data.windows_net_route.default_v4.next_hop` as the gateway address, e.g. in a `precondition` guarding a default-gateway change.

Lookup is by `destination_prefix`, optionally narrowed by `interface_alias` and `next_hop`. Several matches resolve deterministically to the one with the lowest `effective_metric` (`match_count` tells how many matched); zero matches is an error.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Read-only lookup of the current default route. When several match, the one
# with the lowest effective metric wins and match_count tells how many there
# were. Typical use: feed next_hop into a precondition guarding a
# default-gateway change.
data "windows_net_route" "current_default" {
  destination_prefix = "0.0.0.0/0"
}

output "default_gateway" {
  value       = data.windows_net_route.current_default.next_hop
  description = "Gateway address of the winning default route."
}

output "default_match_count" {
  value       = data.windows_net_route.current_default.match_count
  description = "How many default routes matched before the lowest-effective-metric winner was picked."
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `destination_prefix` (String) Route destination in CIDR form (e.g. `"198.51.100.0/24"`, `"0.0.0.0/0"` for the IPv4 default route).

### Optional

- `interface_alias` (String) Restrict the lookup to one interface alias (exact, case-insensitive match).
- `next_hop` (String) Gateway address. As a query input it narrows the lookup; the observed value of the winning route is stored.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `address_family` (String) Address family, as observed on the host (`IPv4` or `IPv6`).
- `effective_metric` (Number) Effective metric Windows uses for route selection (`route_metric` + `interface_metric`), as observed on the host.
- `id` (String) Data source identifier: `<interface_alias>|<destination_prefix>|<next_hop>` of the winning route.
- `interface_index` (Number) Numeric interface index owning the winning route, as observed on the host.
- `interface_metric` (Number) Interface metric from `Get-NetIPInterface`, as observed on the host.
- `match_count` (Number) How many routes matched the lookup before the lowest-effective-metric winner was picked.
- `protocol` (String) Route protocol, as observed on the host (`NetMgmt`, `Dhcp`, `Local`, ...).
- `route_metric` (Number) Route metric of the winning route, as observed on the host.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
